# Flash Physical Read Pipeline — Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the read path of the flash physical controller. It accepts read requests, obtains the requested data from the flash memory, applies the required ECC and de-scrambling operations, and returns the data in the same order in which the requests were accepted.

The module also maintains a small read cache of recently fetched flash words. This cache allows multiple bus-width reads of the same flash word to be satisfied without accessing the flash memory again.

The module does not perform program or erase operations. It observes program/erase activity only to invalidate cached data that would otherwise become stale.

---

## 2. Read Request Acceptance

### 2.1 General behavior

The module shall accept a read request only when it can do so without losing data or violating response ordering. It shall indicate readiness to accept a request only when all internal resources needed to complete that request are available.

Each read request carries the following attributes that affect the read operation:

- The address of the requested bus word.
- Whether the location is scramble-enabled.
- Whether ECC checking is enabled.
- Whether the operation is a read, program, page erase, or bank erase.
- The partition and information-select type.

The module must use the request address to determine the containing flash word. A flash word may contain one or more bus words; the low address bits identify which bus word is requested, and the remaining address bits identify the flash word.

### 2.2 Buffer-hit requests

A request that hits an existing read-buffer entry may be accepted even when the flash memory is still busy with another read, provided that the response-order and staging resources are available.

A request that hits an entry that is still being filled from flash must wait until that fill completes before its response is issued. It must not cause a second flash memory read.

### 2.3 Buffer-miss requests

A request that misses the read buffer must be issued to the flash memory. The module shall accept such a request only when all of the following are true:

- A buffer entry can be allocated.
- The flash read stage is available.
- The read-result and mask staging resources have space.
- The flash memory accepts the read request in the same cycle.

The module shall have at most one flash read outstanding at a time. A new flash read may begin as soon as the previous read completes and its result has been captured.

### 2.4 Buffer disabled

When read buffering is disabled, every read request shall be treated as a buffer miss. No read-buffer lookup or allocation shall be performed, and every request shall be fetched from flash memory.

---

## 3. Response Delivery

The module shall return exactly one response for every accepted read request. Responses shall be returned in the same order as the requests were accepted.

The response handshake is a single-cycle valid pulse. There is no response-ready/backpressure signal; the receiving logic must accept the response whenever the module asserts its data-valid output. Therefore, the module shall assert data-valid only when the response at the head of the response order is fully ready.

The returned data shall be the requested bus-width word selected from the full flash word. The lower address bits captured for that request determine which bus word is returned.

The full-width data output shall include the standard bus-integrity encoding computed over the selected data word. If an in-band error is asserted, the selected data word shall be forced to all ones before the bus-integrity encoding is generated.

---

## 4. Read Buffer Operation

### 4.1 Cache tags and lookup

The read buffer shall store recently read flash words. Each entry shall be tagged with:

- The flash-word-aligned address.
- The partition.
- The information-select type.

A read request is a hit only when its address, partition, and information-select type match an entry. A request to the same address in a different partition or information type shall not hit that entry.

An entry can be in one of the following conceptual states:

- Invalid: the entry does not contain usable data.
- Valid: the entry contains a complete flash word and error status.
- Work-in-progress: a flash read has been issued to fill the entry, but the fill has not yet completed.

### 4.2 Hit behavior

A request that matches a valid entry shall be satisfied from the buffer once it reaches the head of the response order.

A request that matches a work-in-progress entry shall wait for the entry to become valid. All requests already assigned to that entry shall then receive their responses in order.

A valid entry that has a stored reliability error shall not be treated as a hit for new requests. Any requests that were already accepted while the entry was work-in-progress shall still receive the stored error as part of their response.

### 4.3 Allocation and replacement

When a miss needs a new entry, the module shall allocate one according to the following rules:

- An invalid entry shall be preferred.
- A work-in-progress entry shall never be replaced.
- An entry that is still needed by a pending response shall not be replaced.
- If no invalid entry exists, the module shall select among valid entries that are not needed by pending responses using a fair policy.
- If no such entry exists, the module shall not accept the miss until an entry becomes available.

A valid entry with a stored reliability error and no pending response references shall be considered invalid for allocation purposes.

The module shall not accept any new read while every buffer entry is currently referenced by a pending response. It must wait until at least one pending response completes and releases its buffer entry.

### 4.4 Buffer fill

When a flash read completes, the resulting plaintext data and error status shall be written into the allocated buffer entry. The entry shall then become valid.

If the read requires de-scrambling, the buffer shall be updated only after de-scrambling completes.

A buffer entry that receives a reliability multi-bit error shall be marked valid-with-error. This error shall be propagated as an in-band error to every queued response that depends on that entry.

---

## 5. Cache Invalidation on Program/Erase

The module shall invalidate read-buffer entries when stateful operations are presented:

- A program operation targeting a flash word shall invalidate any valid entry with the same flash word address, partition, and information-select type.
- A page erase operation shall invalidate any valid entry whose flash word address falls within the erased page, considering partition and information-select type.
- A bank erase operation shall invalidate all valid buffer entries, regardless of partition or information-select type.

These invalidations ensure that a subsequent read cannot return stale data from before the program/erase operation.

The interface contract requires that program and erase operations be presented only when the read pipeline is idle.

---

## 6. Reliability ECC

The module shall check the raw flash word with the reliability ECC when a flash read completes, if ECC checking is enabled for that read.

### 6.1 Single-bit errors

If a single-bit error is detected and ECC checking is enabled:

- The module shall correct the error before using the data.
- The module shall report the single-bit error event.
- The module shall also provide the flash-word-aligned address associated with the read that produced the error.

The data response itself shall not be flagged as an in-band error for a single-bit error.

### 6.2 Multi-bit errors

If an uncorrectable multi-bit error is detected and ECC checking is enabled:

- The module shall report the event as a reliability ECC error.
- The affected data shall be treated as erroneous.
- All responses that depend on the affected flash read shall receive an in-band error.
- If multiple queued responses depend on the same erroneous fill, each shall receive the in-band error.

The reliability multi-bit error event is reported when the flash read completes, not when the individual responses are delivered.

### 6.3 ECC disabled

When ECC checking is disabled for a read, the module shall not report single-bit or multi-bit reliability errors for that read and shall not use the ECC correction logic to modify the returned data. The data shall still be processed for de-scrambling if required.

---

## 7. Erased Flash Word Handling

A flash word in which all data bits are ones shall be treated as erased.

If a read returns an erased flash word, the module shall skip the de-scrambling stage for that word even if the request’s scramble attribute is set. The erased word shall be forwarded as plaintext data.

Erased-word detection shall not, by itself, suppress reliability ECC processing when ECC is enabled.

---

## 8. De-scrambling

### 8.1 When de-scrambling is required

A read requires de-scrambling when:

- The request’s scramble attribute is set.
- The read misses the buffer.
- The read data is not an erased all-ones flash word.

For a de-scrambling read, the module shall:

- Request calculation of the scrambling mask for the flash-word-aligned address.
- Store the calculated mask until the flash read data is available.
- Present the flash data to the de-scrambling function together with the mask.
- Use the de-scrambled result as the plaintext data for the buffer and for the response.

The mask calculation may be started when the flash read is issued, before the flash data returns, so that mask latency overlaps with flash read latency.

The module shall issue a de-scramble request only when both the flash read data and the calculated mask are available.

### 8.2 When de-scrambling is not required

De-scrambling shall be skipped when:

- The request’s scramble attribute is not set, or
- The flash word is erased.

In these cases, the data read from flash shall be used directly, after any required reliability ECC correction, without waiting for a de-scramble operation.

### 8.3 Overlap

The module shall allow a new flash read to begin while a previous read is still in the de-scrambling stage, provided the necessary staging resources are available. This allows flash reads and de-scrambling to overlap without reordering responses.

---

## 9. Integrity ECC

The module shall check the integrity ECC of the plaintext data before returning a response, if ECC checking is enabled for that response.

This check shall be performed on every response, including responses delivered from the read buffer.

If the integrity check fails:

- The module shall assert an integrity error status output.
- The response shall be flagged as an in-band error.
- The data word returned to the requestor shall be all ones.

If ECC checking is disabled, an integrity mismatch shall not be reported for that response.

---

## 10. Error Reporting Summary

The module shall provide the following error/status outputs:

- A single-bit reliability ECC event indication, with an associated flash-word-aligned address.
- A multi-bit reliability ECC event indication.
- An integrity ECC event indication.
- An in-band data-error indication that accompanies a response.
- An internal queue integrity error indication.

The in-band error indication shall be asserted only when a response is being delivered. It shall be used for all error conditions that make the returned data invalid:

- Uncorrectable reliability ECC errors.
- Integrity ECC mismatches.
- Stored reliability errors propagated from a buffer fill.

For any in-band error, the returned data word shall be all ones before bus-integrity encoding.

The single-bit and multi-bit reliability ECC events shall be reported when the flash read completes. The integrity ECC event shall be reported when the affected response is delivered.

---

## 11. Idle and Configuration

The module shall indicate when the entire read pipeline is idle. It shall be considered idle only when no accepted read remains pending in the response order and no response is waiting to be delivered.

The buffer-enable configuration shall take effect only when the read pipeline is idle. If the configuration input changes while the pipeline is active, the module shall retain its current buffer-enable state until the pipeline becomes idle.

When buffer enable is deasserted, the module shall operate without using the read buffer, as described in Section 2.4.

---

## 12. Internal Error Detection

The module shall monitor its internal queues for storage-integrity failures. If any internal queue reports a corrupted state, the module shall assert the internal queue error output. Such a failure indicates a hardware fault in the module’s internal storage.

# flash_phy_rd_buffers Behavioral Specification

## Overview

This module implements a single read-buffer entry for the flash physical read path.  
The buffer stores the information needed for one flash read transaction:

- the flash word address,
- the partition type (data or information),
- the information select (when the partition is information),
- the read data,
- a read error flag,
- a state indicating whether the entry is unused, being filled, or valid.

The buffer is only a storage element and does not initiate reads. It responds to commands issued by the surrounding read logic.

## Buffer State

The buffer must maintain one of the following states:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Invalid | The entry is unused. Its stored address, data, and error flag are not meaningful. |
| Work-in-Progress (WIP) | The entry has been allocated for a read, but the data has not yet been written. |
| Valid | The entry contains complete read data and can be used to satisfy a request. |

The current state must be observable at the output.

## Reset

On reset:

- The state must become Invalid.
- The address, data, information select, and error flag must be cleared.
- The partition type must be set to the data partition.

## General Command Priority

All commands are evaluated each cycle. If more than one command is active in the same cycle, the buffer must service them in the following order of precedence:

1. Reset
2. Disable (enable deasserted)
3. Wipe
4. Allocate
5. Update

## Enable / Disable

The buffer is only operational while the enable indication is asserted.

When enable is deasserted:

- If the buffer is not already Invalid, it must become Invalid.
- The error flag must be cleared.
- The other stored fields (address, partition, information select, data) may retain their previous values, but they are no longer considered meaningful.

When enable is asserted, normal command processing is allowed.

## Allocation

An allocate command reserves the buffer for a new read transaction.

When enabled and an allocate command is received, and no higher-priority command is active:

- The buffer must capture the supplied address, partition type, and information select.
- The state must become Work-in-Progress.
- The error flag must be cleared.
- The data field is not yet updated; it will be written later by an update command.

An allocate command must not be issued while the buffer is already Work-in-Progress.

## Update

An update command completes a previously allocated read transaction.

When enabled and an update command is received, and no higher-priority command is active:

- The buffer must capture the supplied read data.
- The state must become Valid.
- The error flag must be set to the supplied error status.

An update command must only be issued while the buffer is in the Work-in-Progress state. If the buffer is not Work-in-Progress, the update command is not valid and must not be asserted.

## Wipe

A wipe command invalidates the buffer. This is used when a program or erase operation makes the cached read data stale.

When enabled and a wipe command is received, and no higher-priority command is active:

- The state must become Invalid.
- The error flag must be cleared.
- The stored address, partition, information select, and data may retain their previous values, but they are no longer considered valid.

## Output Behavior

The output must continuously present the current contents of the buffer:

- state,
- address,
- partition type,
- information select,
- data,
- error flag.

After any command takes effect, the output must reflect the new buffer contents.

The output is not required to change in any other way. The data and metadata fields are only meaningful to the rest of the system when the state is Valid.

## Protocol Requirements

To keep the buffer coherent, the surrounding logic must obey these rules:

- An update command must be asserted only when the buffer is in Work-in-Progress state.
- An allocate command must be asserted only when the buffer is not in Work-in-Progress state.
- A wipe command may be asserted at any time.
- All commands are evaluated synchronously with respect to the clock.
